headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading error: B handles secrets and APIs while A is a non-runnable course artifact with no isolation or verification path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a course repo with no runnable surface, while B has stdin/stdout and file inputs but no documented shared channel with A. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or file transfer, so prompt injection is possible but limited and not default. Uncertainty is low because A lacks execution surfaces.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A-generated text into B prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the two, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces.
Do not paste A outputs into B without review.
Use a fixed prompt template for B.
Disable any ad hoc file handoff between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic paper data, and can read/write files plus call APIs. A is a docs-only course artifact with no data classes touched, so the pair does not show direct shared sensitive data, but B's default surfaces can leak its own secrets or paper data if A-derived content is copied into its workspace. The interaction is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF A-derived notes are stored in B's workspace alongside .env or notebooks, leakage risk increases.
IF B sends notebook or file contents to external APIs, sensitive data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Remove secrets from B's working directory.
Store A and B artifacts in separate folders.
Audit B notebooks for API calls before running.
Use placeholder credentials in examples.
Rotate any exposed keys after testing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities and is not runnable, while B can write files and spawn subprocesses but cannot modify git state. There is no documented shared mutable resource or locking conflict between them, so overlap is limited to ordinary local files if an operator manually connects them. The pathway exists only under unusual setup.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator later adds shared state without locks, conflicts can emerge.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one writer at a time.
Snapshot files before B writes.
Avoid sharing git worktrees between agents.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B's course workflow includes agentic RAG notebooks and API endpoints, so it may treat upstream text as authoritative unless the operator adds checks. A is a non-runnable educational repo, but its outputs could still be copied into B's prompts or notebooks, creating a plausible unverified handoff. Because the interaction is inferred from docs rather than observed, uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF A-generated content is used as input to B without a verification step, B may propagate errors.
IF B's agentic-ask or notebook workflows are run on copied A text, downstream actions can reflect those errors.
mitigations: Require human review before B consumes A outputs.
Add a verification checklist for copied content.
Use citations or source links in B prompts.
Log provenance for any A-to-B transfer.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and may process academic papers and metadata, while A is a public course repo with no sensitive data classes. The main compliance issue is B's local-development handling of secrets and API-backed workflows, which can conflict with retention or residency expectations if operators move A-derived materials into B's environment. A is not cited for a residency violation because none is stated.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated data is entered into B's API-backed workflows, residency/compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF secrets remain in notebooks or logs, retention policy violations can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B during testing.
Redact secrets from notebooks and logs.
Use dummy API keys in demos.
Review retention settings before running.
